question.leadin: Following this man's death, hundreds of Spaniards died trying to flee during La Noche Triste [noh-chay tris-tay].
question.text: Name this leader who was allegedly stoned to death by his own people after being taken hostage by conquistadors.
question.answerHtml: Montezuma II (accept Moctezuma II; prompt on “Montezuma” or “Moctezuma” alone)
question.clue: Shortly after this man's death, his people assassinated the rearguard of an invading force in the Night of Sorrows massacre.

swap.text: This Aztec emperor exchanged gifts with Cortez at Cortez's first arrival before his eventual defeat.
swap.clue: Early in his campaign, Cortes captured this Aztec emperor and attempt to rule Mexico through him. The details of this man's captivity and eventual death remain unclear.

question.leadin: The Soviet linguist Yuri Knorozov listed his cat Asya as the co-author of a paper in which he determined that this civilization's writing system was phonetic.
question.text: Name this civilization centered around the Yucatan peninsula whose "long count" calendar had a b'ak'tun end in 2012.
question.clue: The Temple of Inscriptions houses anajaw("ah-how")from this civilizationknown as Pacal the Great who reigned for 68 years in its city-state of Palenque("pah-LEN-kay").

swap.text: The Mayans also constructed a pyramid named El Castillo, or the Temple of Kukulcan, in this city. This city in the Yucatan peninsula also contained the Great Ball Court.
swap.clue: This location was once part of a league with neighboring Uxmal .

question.text: The Colossal Heads were created by this earliest major civilization of Mesoamerica, who were the first to play the mesoamerican ballgame. This culture's writing system may have influenced the later Mayan hieroglyphics system.
question.clue: Much of their art is based on a jaguar god, including much in that capital, La Venta.

swap.leadin: These people were some of the earliest known to populate the Yucatan Peninsula.
swap.text: Name this ancient civilization, which built settlements at La Venta and San Lorenzo, known for its sculptures of large stone heads.
swap.clue: This culture created "elongated man" figurines as well as a greenstone statue of a man holding a were-jaguar ("wair-jaguar").

question.leadin: This group is divided between "highland" and "lowland" cultures, such as the Yucatec.
question.text: Name this people group that named an ancient Mesoamerican civilization of city-states in and around modern-day Guatemala. The city of Chichen Itza was built by this people group.
question.clue: A leader of these people named Pacal the Great ruled Palenque ("PAH-len-kay"), which was abandoned during their supposed 9th-century collapse.

swap.text: This Olmec site became important due to its abundant rainfall, which eliminated the need for an extensive irrigation system. It was located in modern-day Tabasco, and its Great Pyramid, due to erosion, is conical in shape.
swap.clue: Several colossal heads have been found in the sites of San Lorenzo, Tres Zapotes, and Complex B in this Olmec archaeological site in Tabasco. This site also contains the Great Pyramid.

question.text: A ball court can be found at Monte Alban, a city in Oaxaca (wah-HAH-kuh) formerly occupied by the Mixtec and this culture, which carved "danzante" images of captured opponents.
question.clue: The chief god of this culture was the thunder god Cocijo.

swap.leadin: Some "conquest slabs" at this site have been identified at its Building J.
swap.text: Name this archaeological site in Oaxaca, Mexico, the socioeconomic center of the erstwhile Zapotec culture.
swap.clue: Another monument depicts men with scrolls in place of their genitalia who likely represent mutilated war captives - that being the Temple of the Danzantes, or the "Building of the Dancers."

question.leadin: Arthur Anderson and Charles Dibble made the first full English translation of this 12-book work after it was rediscovered by the scholar Angelo Bandini.
question.text: Name this text preserved in the Laurentian library. It was composed by the missionary Bernardino de Sahagun in conjunction with his students in Tlatelolco.
question.clue: Preserved in the Laurentian library, this text provided historians with knowledge about the culture of the Aztec empire. La Malinche or Donna Marina interpreted this text for Hernan Cortes.

swap.leadin: This empire's culture and religion were documented in the Florentine Codex.
swap.text: Name this empire that fought enemies during the Flower Wars. It succeeded in killing numerous outsiders during La Noche Triste, which proved to be only a temporary victory.
swap.clue: Though not the origin of the process, this empire's language is the origin of the word nixtamalization ("NISH-tuh-muhl-uh-zay-shun"), which was typically carried out by the women of this empire.

question.text: After their defeat at Potonchan, the Maya gifted 20 women including this Nahua slave to Hernan Cortes. This woman served as a translator during Cortes' conquest of the Aztecs..
question.answerHtml: La Malinche [or Malintzin; or Doña Marina; or “The Sons of La Malinche”]
question.clue: This woman who, according to legend, gave birth to the first mestizo child in Mexico. This wife of Juan Jaramillo used her mastery of the tecpillatolli dialect of Nahuatl to negotiate with Aztec rulers for the Spanish.

swap.leadin: Naranjo-style pottery suggests that this city may have conquered the distant site Takalik Abaj ("ah-BAH").
swap.text: Name this city whose Pyramid of the Sun flanks its Avenue of the Dead.
swap.clue: The decline of this city has been attributed to an increase in power of the "intermediate elites" by archaeologists such as Linda Manzanilla.

question.leadin: This figure reconquered Cozumel, following the failed attempt a year earlier by Juan de Grijalva and this figure's manipulation of the visit of five tax collectors to Zempoala set the tone for his greatest conquest.
question.text: Name this figure who won the Battle of Otumba against disorganized natives, after his lieutenant, Pedro de Alvarado, had thousands of nobles killed for worshipping Huitzilopochtli during the Toxcatl Massacre.
question.clue: The Florentine Codex details how this man's subordinate, Pedro de Alvarado, massacred most of the people at a festival in the Templo Mayor, leading to the retaliatory murder of this man's soldiers during La Noche Triste.

swap.leadin: These people established a powerful kingdom at Utatlan.
swap.text: Name these people, whose leader Tecun Uman legendarily decapitated Pedro de Alvarado's horse instead of Alvarado while resisting the Spanish at the Battle of El Pinar. Rigoberta Menchu is an activist for the rights of these people.

question.leadin: The ruler of this city, Hunac Ceel, supposedly convinced the ruler at Chichen Itza to steal the bride of Izamal, inciting a war that depopulated Chichen Itza.
question.text: Name this Mesoamerican site in the Yucatan that formed a namesake league of 16 city-states around 1280 AD under the Cocom family, which lasted until the revolt of the Xiu family.

swap.text: The nine books given this name are primary sources on Mayan religious tradition. Among their contents include prophecies and prognostications based on the k'atun cycle and riddles used to confirm public officials for office.

question.leadin: This historian's only written work was used by Tzevtan Todorov to argue that the "site of strategic symbolic occupation" was in the "body of a woman" that appeared in his major text.
question.text: Name this man, who described how the Tlaxcala allied themselves with Hernan Cortes's expedition in his book The True History of the Conquest of New Spain.

swap.leadin: Gardens in this city could only be reached by a flight of 520 marble steps, which referenced the highly significant number of 52 for the people who lived here.
swap.text: What city-state, which was founded in the 12th century, was the second most important member of a Triple Alliance whose least important member was the late-to-join Tlacopan?
swap.clue: This city, likely founded by the Chichimecs, became the capital of the Acolhua after they moved from Coat-linchan.
